evidence.why_not_priced: Only two-to-three analysts cover the name and their numbers are visibly anchored to the guidance, not to the arithmetic: stockanalysis.com shows FY2026 consensus revenue of $966.07M last updated 2026-08-21, which backs into a Q4 revenue of $238.3M, a 5.4% sequential DECLINE from Q3, and the calendar's two Q4 EPS estimates of $0.09 are consistent with a ~$18-20M EBITDA quarter. No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.
evidence.independence: Nine-month revenue of $727.8M is confirmed independently in the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000183437626000022/innv-20260331.htm (filed 2026-05-08), and the Q1 FY26 $17.6M adjusted EBITDA anchor comes from a separate release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/04/3180867/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-First-Quarter-Ended-September-30-2025.html (2025-11-04). evidence.text: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
evidence.why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. What is not on the wire is the mechanism or the size: no published note quantifies the 85%-of-Medicare reset or the 2% July-1 HCBS cut, and the July-1 piece was only confirmed in a state provider bulletin issued a month after InnovAge's last communication. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.
evidence.independence: Independently corroborated by state budget reporting: https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/01/colorado-budget-draft-billion-shortfall-2026/ (2026-04-01, on the ~$1.5bn shortfall and the Medicaid-led cuts) and https://www.vaildaily.com/news/colorado-new-budget-cuts-medicaid/ on the signed budget. expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: US retail registrations on a 12-month rolling basis through June 2026, published 2 September, show the four categories the merged MasterCraft actually competes in are the four weakest in the market - towboats 7,529 units down 9.9%, runabouts 13,261 down 11.4%, pontoons 47,119 down 6.6%, saltwater fishboats 21,523 down 2.8% - against a total market down 3.5% carried by freshwater fishing (+0.4%), while MasterCraft's own nine-month FY26 net sales rose 7.0% to $218.967m on 'higher unit volumes', i.e. it shipped into a channel that was contracting at roughly triple its stated wholesale growth.
evidence.why_not_priced: The read-across everyone did was the wrong one: Brunswick raised FY guidance on a US pipeline down ~1,300 units and Malibu's Q4 net sales rose 42.7% with the stock up 12%, but Malibu's growth is Saxdor (European outboard) and its legacy FY27 guide is only low-to-mid single digit - neither peer's tailwind maps onto towboats, runabouts and pontoons. If the market had priced MCFT's specific mix it would not be sitting on a -6.2% twenty-day run-up with sell-side targets of $25-$30 raised into a sector rally, and there would be a note reconciling a +7% wholesale build against a -9.9% towboat retail number. The transition-period guide is the first moment the company has to reconcile the two.
